title: Kinetic and potential energy; conservation; Work done; Work–energy theorem and dissipative forces; Gravitational potential and energy
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: E02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; E02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; E01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; E02-ap1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C04-1#N.9b, C04-2#N.4, E01-1#N.5, E02-1#N.4a, E02-ap1#N.2, E04-1#N.3, C04-2#N.5, E01-1#N.9a, E02-1#N.12, E04-1#N.6c, C04-2#N.6b, E04-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mechanical energy
items.clue: Sum that stays constant when there is no friction or drag.

items.label: Gravitational potential energy
items.clue: Store that depends on position, lost as a dropped ball speeds up.

items.label: Component
items.clue: Part of a force along the displacement: the only part that transfers energy.

items.label: Energy bar chart
items.clue: Diagram with one column each for K, U_g and U_s at the start and end, plus W.

questions.stem: A probe is moved from a distance R to a distance 3R from the center of a planet of radius R. What fraction of the energy needed to move it from R all the way to infinity is this?
questions.explanation: To infinity: GMm/R. From R to 3R: GMm(1/R − 1/3R) = (2/3)GMm/R. Fraction 2/3.

questions.stem: A probe is launched straight up from the surface of a planet with exactly the escape speed. The planet has no atmosphere, its motion is negligible, and the only force exerted on the probe after launch is the planet's gravitational force. Which statement describes the probe's motion after launch?

options.text: It slows down until it is beyond the reach of gravity, then moves at a constant speed.
It slows to a stop at a large but finite distance, then falls back to the planet.
It slows down all the time, its speed approaching zero as its distance approaches infinity.
It speeds up as it moves away, since U_g decreases as its distance increases.

questions.stem: A worker uses a rope to lower a box straight down at constant speed. Which statement about the work done on the box during the descent is correct?

options.text: The tension does positive work and gravity does negative work on the box.
The tension does negative work and gravity does positive work.
The tension and gravity both do positive work on the box as it moves.
Neither force does any work, as the box's speed does not change.

questions.stem: Object A has mass m and moves at speed 2v. Object B has mass 2m and moves at speed v. What is the kinetic energy of object A divided by the kinetic energy of object B?
questions.explanation: A: ½m(2v)² = 2mv². B: ½(2m)v² = mv². So A has twice B's kinetic energy: doubling the speed multiplies it by 4, doubling the mass only by 2.

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg ball rolls forward along the floor of a train car at 2.0 m s⁻¹ relative to the car. The train moves along a straight, level track at a constant 20 m s⁻¹ relative to the ground. What is the ball's kinetic energy as measured by an observer standing beside the track?
questions.explanation: Relative to the ground the ball moves at 20 + 2.0 = 22 m s⁻¹ (both forward). K = ½ × 0.50 × 22² = 121 J.

questions.stem: A child on a toboggan slides across level snow. The child and toboggan have a total mass of 50 kg and slow down from 8.0 m s⁻¹ to 6.0 m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the net work done on the child–toboggan system during this time?

A 500 kg probe is launched from the surface of a moon of mass 7.3 × 10²² kg and radius 1.7 × 10⁶ m. The moon has no atmosphere and its motion is negligible. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². What is the escape speed from the moon's surface?

A car drives at constant speed around a flat circular bend of radius 50 m. The friction force from the road on the car is 4000 N and acts towards the centre of the bend. How much work does this force do on the car while it goes a quarter of the way around?

options.text: About 3.1 × 10⁵ J, the force multiplied by the length of the arc.
About 2.0 × 10⁵ J, the force multiplied by the radius of the bend.
Zero, as the force is perpendicular to the car's velocity.
A negative amount, as friction always takes energy away from a car.

questions.explanation: θ = 90° throughout, so the work (force × displacement × cos θ) is zero. The speed, and so the kinetic energy, does not change, which agrees.

questions.stem: Three identical stones are thrown from the top of a sea cliff with the same speed: one straight up, one horizontally and one straight down. Air resistance is negligible. Which stone hits the sea with the greatest speed?

options.text: The one thrown straight down, as its velocity starts in the direction of gravity.
The one thrown upwards, as it falls back from a greater height than the others.
The one thrown horizontally, as it keeps its horizontal speed while gaining vertical speed.
All land at equal speeds: same starting kinetic energy, same drop in height.

questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy + potential energy lost = final kinetic energy, and both terms are equal for all three stones. The speeds are equal; only the directions and times of flight differ.

questions.stem: A 5.0 kg box slides 4.0 m down a ramp inclined at 37° to the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the box and the ramp is 0.25. Use g = 10 m s⁻², sin 37° = 0.60 and cos 37° = 0.80. How much mechanical energy is dissipated by friction during the slide?

A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius r around a planet with speed v₀. The planet's motion is negligible. Which expression gives the escape speed at the distance r from the planet's center, in terms of v₀?
A person pushes a box across a rough, level floor at constant speed. The system is the box and the floor. Which statement correctly describes the change in the total energy of the system?

options.text: It does not change, as the box keeps moving at a constant speed.
It does not change, as friction removes the energy that the push adds.
It decreases, as friction destroys energy while the box slides.
It increases, as the person's push does positive work on the system.
